name: Letterpress Printing
visualIdentity: Supplemental printmaking reference, not a source-collection style claim. Thick cream paper, shallow debossed edges, natural dark ink coverage, simple typography and graphics, and soft side lighting reveal the impression.
suitableUses: Use for short typographic statements and stationery. Editorial grids can extend it to literary promos, publisher brands, and report covers; restrained macro presentation suits invitations, business cards, and craft stationery. These are inferred fits.
limitations: Avoid metallic bevels, deep embossing, heavy blur, gold sparkle, and sliding whole pages. Keep impressions shallow and uniform, ink discrete, and body copy as real text in HTML. Omit chapter transitions when they obscure causality, break a continuous shot or loop, or add needless boundaries.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: cream paper #F6EDD9 background, dark ink #343932 foreground, and restrained oxblood #914839 accent. Three discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Exact task, brand, or approved reference colors take precedence. Preserve color roles, asset colors, and ink limits; texture and lighting do not license extra spot colors. Check contrast in the actual composite.
motionAndInteraction: Use restrained typesetting, pressing, or localized reveals; keep transitions and reading holds deliberate. For video, drive all states from seekable composition time. For interactive HTML, scroll can scrub finite chapter handoffs or ordered story stages; reverse and direct seeks must restore coherent states. Pattern candidates are optional and need scene-level justification. Avoid generic smoothing and unsupported motion.
audio: Unspecified; choose per topic and user requirements. Music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence are optional, not style rules. Synchronize any chosen audio with picture, preserve speech clarity, and check the final mix for clipping and balance.
assetRequirements: Use thick paper and glyph or graphic outlines to create shallow impressions; control paper texture, ink coverage, impression depth, and soft side lighting separately. Load local fonts and assets. Distinguish simulated print from photographed production; exact copy and supplied artwork retain their colors and wording.
combinations: Alone for concise typography and stationery. With style-019 editorial grid and serif/sans hierarchy for longer reading order; keep oxblood to one element. With style-096 slow macro camera and selective reveal for printed-object launches. These pairings are suggestions; retain shallow impressions, side light, and minimal page movement.
productionApproach: Choose visual rendering and motion methods for fidelity first; Blender/bpy with Cycles or EEVEE can create materials, lighting, and motion. HyperFrames owns assembly, seekable timing, sync, validation, and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded. Keep layers deterministic and inspect actual frames and the full video. For HTML, use real text and static/reduced-motion states; scroll behavior is interactive only.
